about: Every tunable weight in the projection, in one editable file.
The engine reads its defaults from here, so changing a number here changes
the recommendation — no code edit, no rebuild of anything but the bundle.
Each block carries a `why` recording what evidence set the number, because a
weight with no provenance is a guess, and this project does not ship guesses.
Re-measure any change with `nub run compete --seasons=2021,2022,2023,2024,2025 --moves=1`.
Season win/loss counts decide; ranking correlation is advisory only.

why: volumeWeight 0.75: playing time is the single largest edge available, worth ~20% relative Spearman over a season-only estimate.
blend 0.5/0.5: chosen by playing seasons, not by correlation. A 14-day ranking mildly preferred 0.75; five played seasons prefer 0.5 by ~1,500 points and seven weekly wins.
rate: pitchers only, and lightly — 41 of 50 folds. The same blend for hitters won 29 of 50, a coin flip, so it is not applied.
windows: the last series is worth more than the fortnight before it. Pitchers work a five-day turn, so their short window is 5 days rather than 3.

weight 0 is STALE, not justified. It was set by a measurement that ran on leaked data — Savant's custom leaderboard ignores its own date parameters and returns the finished season. On real point-in-time data xwOBA out-predicts wOBA (rho 0.1019 vs 0.0581 over 5,151 player-weeks) and the gap adds significant incremental signal (partial rho +0.0944, z 6.79).
Re-derive this with `nub run compete --statcast-real` before trusting it either way — correlation and played seasons have disagreed here before.

windowDays 21: the signal was measured on a rolling three-week window, not on season-to-date. Contact and results diverge far more inside three weeks (gap~wOBA -0.61) than across a season (-0.36), and that divergence is the whole signal. 0 means season-to-date.
lambda.mode 'rising' trusts xwOBA MORE as batted-ball sample grows; 'falling' trusts it more in SMALL samples, which is what the stabilisation literature actually argues; 'fixed' ignores sample.

scope 'wide' scales runs and RBI along with the batted-ball events; 'battedBall' leaves run production alone, on the grounds that a hitter's runs depend on the eight men around him, not on his contact quality.
Who a player actually faces this week, from the real schedule: a hitter is scaled by the quality of the staffs he is booked against, a pitcher by the lineups.
Opponent strength is measured from the same leak-free prior window as everything else — never from what the opponent went on to do.

weight 0.5 is the conservative end of a real but unproven effect. Across 111 paired weeks the gain is monotone in the weight (+69 pts at 0.1 up to +548 at 1.0) and positive at every dose, but no dose is statistically significant on its own: head to head against weight 0, 0.5 goes 51W-44L-16T (+1.8/wk) and 1.0 goes 59W-49L-3T (+4.9/wk).
When a dose-response is monotone but no single dose clears significance, the smallest dose that shows the effect risks the least. Raise it to 1.0 if you want the measured maximum.
Savant park factors, applied over the venues on the horizon schedule rather than as a season-long team constant.
Roughly the volume at which a stat is half signal, half noise, following the published stabilisation work (Carleton / Tango).
`default` is deliberately heavy: an unlisted stat is one we have no stabilisation evidence for, and heavy shrinkage is the honest response to that.
